messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: node.local-7 disk usage > 94% (root=/var/lib/kubelet). Multiple pods being Evicted. Auto-escalation to #incidents. paging @Asha :rotating_light:

Asha: I saw the alert, joining. Can someone post the initial error from the runtime pods?

Sam: root cause looks like model cache + rotated logs filled /var/lib/kubelet on the node. From one of the runtime pods: 
```
2026-03-15T09:04:12Z runtime ERROR: write /var/lib/kubelet/pods/abc123/volumes/kubernetes.io~empty-dir/model-cache/model-7.bin: no space left on device
2026-03-15T09:04:12Z runtime FATAL: exiting due to disk write error
```

Jordan: also seeing kubelet evict logs: 
```
Mar 15 09:05:01 kubelet eviction-manager: eviction threshold reached: resource available < eviction threshold (imagefs.available < 10%)
Mar 15 09:05:02 kubelet: eviction: Pod default/runtime-xyz evicted
```

Devin: df from node.local-7: 
```
NAME                    SIZE  USED  AVAIL  USE%  MOUNTED ON
/dev/nvme0n1p1          300G  295G    1G   97%   /var/lib/kubelet
```

Asha: OK — impact? Any 5xxs or customer reports?

Beth: CustomerSuccess: we have two customers (acme-inc, finlytics) reporting elevated inference errors/timeout at 09:05 UTC. Tickets created. Sending short status to them: "We're investigating an infrastructure issue causing intermittent errors; engineers are mitigating now."

Sam: Runtime logs also show a CUDA error when the container restarted mid-evict: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` for a few restart attempts. Likely the node flapped during GPU init because the pod crashed while writing cache.

Asha: I'm going to do a controlled cordon/drain of node.local-7, and we need to avoid scheduling more model-heavy pods on similar nodes. Jordan, can you confirm drain command and quick migration?

Jordan: running: 
```bash
kubectl cordon node.local-7
kubectl drain node.local-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=60
```
Note: using `--delete-emptydir-data` will remove emptyDir volumes (which is our model-cache). We'll need to rehydrate model caches after migration.

Devin: Creating a temporary PVC-backed model-cache class on nodepool with bigger rootfs would be slower. Short-term patch: adjust runtime to reduce cache retention and enable on-startup model lazy-load to avoid huge prefetch. Sam, can you patch the deployment?

Sam: Pushing a patch to reduce cache size and disable prefetch. Rolling update command: 
```bash
kubectl set env deploy/runtime --containers=runtime RUNTIME_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=1073741824 RUNTIME_PREFETCH=false
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime
```

Asha: While rollout happens, Jordan please remove node.local-7 from schedulable. Sam, after rollout, migrate a few pods manually to confirm stability.

Jordan: cordon + drain complete. Pods moved off node.local-7. Observed some restarts but no further ENOSPC after drain.

Sam: After patch, new pods start with smaller cache. Example log: 
```
2026-03-15T09:18:10Z runtime INFO: cache max set to 1GB, prefetch disabled
2026-03-15T09:18:42Z runtime INFO: model loaded lazily, first request took 2.6s
```

Asha: Monitoring: disk pressure alerts cleared for node.local-7 after kubelet reclaimed data. But note: /var/lib/kubelet usage still high on several nodes with older images and model caches.

Devin: Immediate mitigation plan: 
- rotate/compress old runtime logs in /var/log/pods (enable logrotate)
- enforce emptyDir size limit on model-cache mount (k8s ephemeral-storage requests/limits)
- create a small PVC-backed cache option (medium-term)

I'll open PRs for logrotate and pod ephemeral-storage limits.

Beth: Customer update: Sent to acme-inc + finlytics: "We mitigated an infrastructure storage pressure event that caused short-lived inference errors between 09:04-09:18 UTC. Services are stable; we will follow up with a postmortem and any risk mitigation steps."

Asha: Quick impact summary for on-call handoff: 
- incident start: 1795001234 (09:04 UTC)
- affected infra: node.local-7 primary, some spillover on node.local-3
- customer impact: transient 5xx/timeouts for acme-inc, finlytics; ~14 minutes
- mitigation: cordon/drain node.local-7, reduced runtime cache, rolled runtime deploy, enabled logrotate follow-up
- next steps: Jordan/Devin/Sam to include sizing docs and limit enforcement; Beth will notify customers when postmortem ready.

Jordan: I'll add a temporary cluster-level alert for imagefs.available < 15% and a runbook step to check emptyDir usage.

Sam: Postmortem checklist items I'll handle: ensure runtime checks for ENOSPC and fall back to reduced-cache mode instead of crashing; add safe-start gating on available disk before prefetching.

Devin: I'll schedule a maintenance window to roll nodes with small rootfs and expand root volumes where feasible.

Asha: Handoff to night oncall @Jordan at 09:30 UTC — Jordan, you have it. If anything flares up, page me.

Jordan: acknowledged, taking over.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: severity=high -> mitigated; follow-up required. Created incident-1795001234 in ops incident tracker.

Asha: Thanks all. We'll write a short postmortem and link to this thread.
